## Why This Is Asked
In real deployments, multilingual users mix languages mid-discussion. This tests practical skill in diagnosing and mitigating tokenization-driven attention issues.

## Key Concepts
- Transformer attention with streaming/multi-language inputs
- Tokenization impact on cross-language semantics
- Simple boundary-aware attention reweighting

## Code Example
```python
import numpy as np

def kl(p, q):
    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float); q = np.asarray(q, dtype=float)
    p = p / p.sum(); q = q / q.sum()
    return float(np.sum(np.where(p>0, p * np.log(p/q), 0)))
# toy: 4 heads per chunk, compute drift between chunks
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you isolate tokenizer effects from model weights?
- What data/loss tweaks would you try to reduce cross-language drift?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests building a robust safety-grounding evaluation across domains, focusing on refusals and escalations, not just factual accuracy.

## Key Concepts
- Grounding verification against versioned docs
- Refusal strategy and escalation policies
- Cross-domain drift tracking
- Evaluation datasets across three domains

## Code Example
```javascript
// Baseline evaluator sketch: compute simple grounding score against a reference doc list
function groundingScore(citations, refs) {
  // citations: array of cited doc ids; refs: set of valid ids
  let hits = citations.filter(c => refs.has(c)).length
  return hits / Math.max(1, citations.length)
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- What latency and cost trade-offs arise when validating citations against live docs in real-time?

## Why This Is Asked
Real-world knowledge bases demand fast, accurate multilingual retrieval with robust chunking and freshness. This question probes architecture, trade-offs, and evaluable metrics.

## Key Concepts
- Multilingual embeddings and cross-encoder reranking
- Document chunking strategies (size, overlap)
- Vector databases and provenance metadata
- Delta updates for freshness and privacy controls
- End-to-end evaluation (NDCG@k, recall@k, latency)

## Code Example
```python
# Simple chunk generator
def chunk_text(text, max_tokens=1024, overlap=200):
    chunks = []
    start = 0
    while start < len(text):
        end = min(start + max_tokens, len(text))
        chunks.append(text[start:end])
        start = end - overlap
    return chunks
```

## Follow-up Questions
